text: Vietnam eliminates mobile coverage gaps for over 130,000 people in remote areas

After more than seven months of implementation, 1,337 new base stations, installed by Viettel, have brought high-speed mobile connectivity to approximately 130,000 people across remote 788 villages and hamlets, as well as 1,068 residential clusters with populations of more than 50 residents each.
The project has increased Viettel's nationwide mobile coverage rate to 99.7% of the population.

On November 20, the Ministry of National Defense held a conference to review the 2026 Mobile Coverage Expansion Program for underserved villages, hamlets, and residential communities in remote, border, and mountainous areas.
Politburo Resolution 57 identifies digital infrastructure as a key foundation for Vietnam's national digital transformation, with citizens at its center.

To implement this policy, in March 2026, the Prime Minister assigned the Ministry of National Defense to direct Viettel to eliminate mobile coverage gaps in remote, border, and hard-to-reach areas within the year.

The initiative was considered the most challenging remaining task after more than three decades of mobile network development in Vietnam, as the uncovered locations are scattered across mountainous and border regions with rugged terrain that is often inaccessible to motorized vehicles.
According to Viettel, the company simultaneously carried out site surveys, network design, site acquisition, and equipment preparation beginning in March 2026.
Connectivity solutions were selected based on local terrain conditions.

These included 3,800 km of fiber-optic cable and 10,000 transmission poles in areas where cable deployment was feasible, 170 microwave transmission routes in locations where fiber installation was impossible, and low-Earth-orbit satellite connectivity for the most isolated communities.
For sites without access to the national power grid, electricity was provided through more than 600 km of newly constructed power lines and solar energy systems.
The program's overarching objective was to deliver social benefits.
Mobile connectivity enables residents in mountainous regions to receive timely disaster warnings and allows students to access online learning resources.
In border areas, 48 newly installed stations are supporting border guard forces in patrol operations and border management.
Speaking at the conference, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, General Phan Van Giang, asked Viettel to ensure the stable and secure operation of the infrastructure system.
He also emphasized the need for contingency plans covering equipment, materials, and local power supplies to guarantee uninterrupted communications under all circumstances.
